Pin GitHub Actions to digest for security

`.tool-versions` is read by asdf, which installs Node through node-build — and node-build adds a definition DAYS after nodejs.org publishes a release. Renovate resolves Node from nodejs.org and knows nothing about node-build, so it offers versions asdf cannot install: 26.9.0 was published 2026-09-16, raised and automerged here on 2026-09-19, and four days later `asdf install nodejs 26.9.0` still fails with `definition not found`. Until it lands, no local checkout can install the pinned Node, so `just generate` and every other Node task dies with `No version is set for command node`. CI is unaffected — actions/setup-node resolves from nodejs.org too. Hence both settings: wait for node-build to catch up, and never automerge the one file that decides whether local Node works at all. The 7 days is now MEASURED rather than guessed — across all 13 Node 26.x releases the nodejs.org-to-node-build lag was median 1 day, mean 2.1, max 9, with ten of thirteen inside a single day and the three outliers (6, 7, 9) all from May and June. 7 days covers twelve of the thirteen. It cannot cover all of them and no number can: the lag is unbounded, and 26.9.0 sat at four days and counting against a recent norm of one. So the delay only reduces how often a PR arrives that cannot be applied locally; `automerge: false` is what actually stops one landing unread. See #364.

A DaisyUI bump moves the submodule tag and regenerates every component, so it always needs a human on the generated diff — never automerge. No version cap: the 5.5.22 ceiling came from codegen/src/parser/llms-txt.js requiring a static llms.txt that DaisyUI deleted in 5.5.23, and the parser now falls back to daisyui/skills/daisyui/components/. Renovate resolves this through the webjar coordinate in gradle/libs.versions.toml, so it only ever offers a version whose CSS artifact actually exists.
